requirements.evidence: Nearly all shapes are present (Entity.php:11-31, UserRole.php:4-12, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:9-33) but the code cannot load and the migration cannot run: app/Models/Entity.php:7 and app/Models/EntityMembership.php:6 import `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\HasFactory` (the trait lives in `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\HasFactory`), database/migrations/2026_10_29_000000_create_entities_table.php:15 chains `->unique()->index('entities_slug_unique')`, producing two indexes with the same name, and database/factories/EntityMembershipFactory.php:16 calls `Entity::factory()` without importing `App\Models\Entity`. The task's explicit doc requirement (`Read docs/database-schema.md and update it`) is also unmet: the file never appears in change.diff.

conventions.evidence: Policies live in app/Policies (EntityPolicy.php:9, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:8) and `$fillable` is set deliberately (Entity.php:13-16, EntityMembership.php:15-19), which is on-convention. But migrations are hand-written in the old named-class style with no return types (2026_10_29_000000_create_entities_table.php:8-23, 2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:8-30) instead of `make:migration`'s anonymous class, models use `$casts`/`$fillable` properties while sibling app/Models/User.php uses `casts()` and `#[Fillable]` (EntityMembership.php:22-24), `docs/database-schema.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` were not updated (conventions.md:92-103), and no test was written first (conventions.md:12-21).

security.evidence: Authorization is correctly centralised in policies and checks membership server-side (EntityPolicy.php:16-36, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:9-33); `delete` blocks the owner membership before the self-removal shortcut (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:24-29), and `manageSettings` is owner-only (EntityPolicy.php:33). Gaps: `assignRole` only checks that the actor is owner/admin and never protects the owner's membership (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:18-28, comment at :28 'Not specified; allow'), so an admin can demote the owner and then take ownership; and `role`/`user_id`/`entity_id` are mass-assignable (EntityMembership.php:15-19), including the privileged `owner` value. No Livewire/Blade/unescaped-output concerns in this diff.

tests.evidence: change.diff contains only models, enum, policies, factories and two migrations; no tests/ changes at all (full diff ends at 393 lines after the entity_memberships migration). No coverage of the one-owner constraint, the policy matrix (owner/admin/employee/non-member), self-removal or the factory states, despite conventions.md:12-21 making tests mandatory for every feature.

simplicity.evidence: The change is small and direct (35-line Entity, 44-line policy), but `User::membershipFor()` exists (User.php:35-38) yet three policies re-implement the same lookup as `$entity->memberships()->where('user_id', ...)` (EntityPolicy.php:18,24,34; EntityMembershipPolicy.php:21,30), and the slug index is requested twice (2026_10_29_000000_create_entities_table.php:15). Redundant same-namespace imports and an unused `Auth` import (EntityMembership.php:7-11) are extra noise.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods are short, but app/Models/EntityMembership.php:11 repeats `use App\Models\UserRole;`, which is a PHP fatal ('Cannot use ... because the name is already in use'), and the unused `Auth` import (:7) plus five redundant same-namespace imports (:8-11) are dead code. `EntityPolicy::create` compares a non-nullable parameter to null (EntityPolicy.php:14), and `EntityMembershipPolicy::assignRole` ends with a speculative comment instead of a decided rule (:28).

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: app/Models/{Entity,EntityMembership,UserRole}.php, the User relation additions (User.php:35-48), app/Policies/{Entity,EntityMembership}Policy.php, both factories and both migrations. No routes, Livewire, session or UI code, and no unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: Imports `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\HasFactory`, which does not exist (the trait is `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\HasFactory`), so `use HasFactory` at line 9 triggers a fatal 'trait not found' and the Entity model — and therefore `Entity::factory()` — cannot be loaded.
Same wrong `HasFactory` namespace as Entity.php, so the EntityMembership model fatals on load; combined with the duplicate import on line 11 this file cannot even be compiled.
`use App\Models\UserRole;` is declared twice (lines 10 and 11), which PHP 8 rejects at compile time with 'Cannot use App\Models\UserRole as UserRole because the name is already in use'.

`$table->string('slug')->unique()->index('entities_slug_unique')` asks for a unique index (whose default name is already `entities_slug_unique`) plus a second index with that same explicit name, so the migration fails with a duplicate index/key name on both SQLite and MariaDB; it should be `->unique('entities_slug_unique')`.

Calls `Entity::factory()` but only imports `App\Models\EntityMembership` and `App\Models\User`, so it resolves to the non-existent `Database\Factories\Entity` and every membership a test tries to create throws 'Class not found'.
The task explicitly requires updating `docs/database-schema.md` (it still documents the replaced `owner_membership_id` FK) and the diff does not touch it, leaving the schema documentation wrong.
No Pest/PHPUnit tests ship with the change, so the one-owner constraint, the policy matrix, self-removal and factory states are entirely unverified, contrary to the project's test-first rule.

`assignRole` grants owner/admin the ability to change any membership's role, including the owner's membership, so an admin can demote the owner and then promote themselves to owner — a privilege escalation and a break of the one-owner invariant that `manageSettings` relies on.

`role`, `entity_id` and `user_id` are all fillable, so any array passed to `create()`/`update()` can set the privileged `owner` role or re-point a membership to another user/entity; narrower fillable or guarded assignment would be safer.

Migrations use the legacy named-class form with untyped `up()`/`down()` instead of the anonymous-class file produced by `php artisan make:migration`, which points to hand-written migrations the conventions forbid.
Conventions require a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `[Unreleased]` for behaviour changes; the diff adds none.

Uses a `protected $casts` property while the sibling `User` model uses the `casts()` method (and Entity uses `$fillable` while User uses `#[Fillable]`), so the new models do not match the existing style.
The membership lookup is duplicated in five places (EntityPolicy.php:18,24,34 and EntityMembershipPolicy.php:21,30) even though `User::membershipFor()` already exists and is used in the view policy.

Unused `Auth` import plus redundant imports of classes in the same `App\Models` namespace add dead code; Entity.php also has a second copy of the mis-namespaced HasFactory import (line 7) that is never used correctly.
`create()` returns `$user !== null` for a non-nullable `User` parameter, which is always true; `return true;` states the rule (any authenticated user) more clearly.

review.summary: The change adds the intended Entity/EntityMembership models, UserRole enum, policies, factories and migrations, and the structure broadly matches the contract, but both model files fatal on PHP (wrong HasFactory namespace and a duplicate `use` statement), the entities migration requests the same index name twice, and the membership factory references an unimported class. On top of that the one-owner constraint, policies and factories ship with no tests and `docs/database-schema.md` was never updated, and `assignRole` lets an admin demote the owner. The change cannot run as delivered, so it is rejected.
